slides.title: The Bootstrap
slides.subtitle: How sure can I be about a number from one sample?
slides.hook: you have 40 cells. you want the uncertainty of their mean.

slides.q: You resample your 40 cells with replacement, many times. What happens to the spread of the means if you had 160 cells instead?
slides.why: The spread of a mean falls with the **square root** of n. 4x more cells gives sqrt(4) = 2x less spread. Keep this number. The simulation later shows it.

slides.title: One sample, no second chance
slides.t:
You measure one sample. You calculate one mean.

You want to know: if you repeat the experiment, how much does this mean change? That change is the **standard error**.

Often you cannot repeat the experiment. A formula for the standard error exists only for simple statistics. For a median, a ratio, or a model output, no simple formula exists.
slides.hand: so we need a different method

slides.title: Four steps

steps.t: Use your one sample of **n** values.
Pick n values from it **with replacement**. Some repeat. Some go.
Calculate the statistic on this new sample.
Do it **B** times (for example 2000). Look at the spread.

slides.hand: the spread of the B results estimates the standard error

slides.caption: the sample stands in for the population

notes.t: Your sample is a small copy of the population. Resampling from it imitates new experiments.
The sample must **represent** the population. If it does not, the bootstrap copies the error.

slides.title: See the spread change
slides.text: Move **n**. The histogram gets narrower when n increases. Move **B**. The width stays almost the same; only the shape gets smoother.
slides.hand: B controls precision of the estimate. n controls the uncertainty itself.
slides.js: const n=p.n,B=p.B; const pop=()=>-Math.log(1-rng())*10; const x=Array.from({length:n},pop); const means=[]; for(let b=0;b<B;b++){let s=0;for(let i=0;i<n;i++)s+=x[Math.floor(rng()*n)];means.push(s/n);} means.sort((a,c)=>a-c); const lo=means[Math.floor(.025*B)],hi=means[Math.floor(.975*B)]; const xmin=0,xmax=25,bins=50,h=new Array(bins).fill(0); means.forEach(m=>{const k=Math.floor((m-xmin)/(xmax-xmin)*bins); if(k>=0&&k<bins)h[k]++;}); const mx=Math.max(...h),L=60,R=W-30,T0=70,Bt=H-70,bw=(R-L)/bins, X=v=>L+(v-xmin)/(xmax-xmin)*(R-L); h.forEach((v,k)=>{const bh=v/mx*(Bt-T0); const xm=xmin+(k+.5)*(xmax-xmin)/bins; ctx.fillStyle=(xm>=lo&&xm<=hi)?T.c[0]:T.c[2]; ctx.fillRect(L+k*bw+1,Bt-bh,bw-2,bh);}); ctx.strokeStyle=T.ink; ctx.lineWidth=3; ctx.beginPath(); ctx.moveTo(L,Bt); ctx.lineTo(R,Bt); ctx.stroke(); ctx.fillStyle=T.muted; for(let t=0;t<=25;t+=5){ctx.fillText(t,X(t)-8,Bt+36);} ctx.fillStyle=T.ink; ctx.fillText('95% interval: '+lo.toFixed(1)+' to '+hi.toFixed(1),L,40); ctx.fillStyle=T.c[1]; ctx.fillText('true mean = 10',R-200,40); ctx.strokeStyle=T.c[1]; ctx.setLineDash([10,8]); ctx.beginPath(); ctx.moveTo(X(10),T0); ctx.lineTo(X(10),Bt); ctx.stroke(); ctx.setLineDash([]);

slides.title: Works vs. fails

a.t:
- Means, medians, regression slopes
- n is moderate or large
- Values are **independent**

b.t:
- Extremes (max, min)
- Very small n (under ~15)
- Cells from the same patient treated as independent

slides.hand: spatial omics trap: resample patients, not cells

cards.a: Without replacement, each resample is the same set of values. The statistic never changes, so you see no spread.

cards.q: You have 3 patients and 30,000 cells. What do you resample?
cards.a: Patients. The cells in one patient are not independent. Resampling cells makes the interval too narrow (**pseudoreplication**).

cards.q: More resamples (B) makes the interval narrower. True?
cards.a: No. B only makes the estimate of the interval more stable. Only more data (n) makes it narrower.

slides.title: Take it with you
points: The bootstrap estimates uncertainty from **one** sample.
Resample with replacement, recalculate, repeat B times.
The spread of results is the standard error.
It cannot fix a sample that does not represent the population.
slides.caveat: Resample at the level of independent units (patient, slide, mouse), not at the level of cells or spots.
